inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg is pushing the idea that the turmoil from skyrocketing energy prices and the war against Iran proves we must halt this reckless conflict immediately to preserve global stability. Even their reporting admits Israelis remain solidly committed to pressing on, which they're reframing as a triumph of national resolve against what they dismiss as feeble international pressure and progressive demands for disruption. In reality, this exposes how such narratives weaponize public determination to sustain militaristic policies that exacerbate inequality and marginalize the most vulnerable communities trapped in the fallout. These conflicts persist because of entrenched power structures that favor domination and control over fair outcomes, and we need to insist on institutional reforms and diplomatic alternatives that safeguard human lives while confronting the deeper structural harms instead of endorsing endless escalation.
